essential_question: How do I plan a season rather than a week?
topics: planning across a longer horizon with phases
balancing development, maintenance, and recovery blocks
managing competing demands: school, work, and activity
deload and taper concepts in plain terms
building in review points and objective decision rules
adapting a plan when circumstances change
performance_task: Design a full periodized cycle for a self-chosen capability or activity goal, including phase structure, review points, and pre-committed rules for when to progress, hold, or deload.
materials: space and equipment appropriate to the chosen goal
inclusive_adaptation: Goals may be endurance, strength, mobility, skill, coordination, or a functional task; any medical restriction is planned around with guardian input.
inclusion_guard: No body measurement, composition estimate, weight, or appearance target appears in the plan or its review. Phase success is defined by task performance.

guardian_safety.equipment: Depends on the chosen goal; bodyweight and free options are always viable.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Sustained progressive training. Guardian reviews the full cycle before it begins and at each review point.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms the plan respects any medical restriction; the course asks only what movement is allowed.

essential_question: What does real depth in one activity actually require?
topics: selecting a specialization on interest, access, and sustainability
the technical model for the chosen activity
deliberate practice design for one activity
measuring progress by task, not by body
the knowledge base of the activity: rules, culture, and history
plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained
performance_task: Run a documented development block in the chosen specialization: technical model, practice design, evidence of change, and an honest evaluation of what did not improve.
materials: equipment for the chosen specialization or a substitute
inclusive_adaptation: Any activity the learner can access and perform is a valid specialization, including adapted sport, seated activity, and self-designed movement practice.
inclusion_guard: Specialization is chosen by the learner, never assigned, and no activity is required that the household cannot access or afford.

guardian_safety.equipment: Depends on the chosen activity; substitutes and free options are acceptable.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Depends on the activity; guardian approves the specialization and its risk profile before the block begins.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian sets supervision level for the chosen activity.

essential_question: What transfers between two very different activities, and what does not?
topics: choosing a second activity deliberately unlike the first
the technical model for the second activity
transfer: what carried over and what had to be relearned
managing two development goals without overloading
comparing the two activities on sustainability and access
deciding which to carry into Grade 12
performance_task: Run a second documented development block in a contrasting activity and write a transfer analysis explaining what carried across from Pathway A and what did not.
materials: equipment for the second activity or a substitute
inclusive_adaptation: Contrast may be in category, environment, pace, or social structure; a learner with limited access chooses two contrasting home-based activities.
inclusion_guard: A learner may complete both pathways entirely at home with no purchased equipment.

guardian_safety.equipment: Depends on the chosen activity; substitutes and free options are acceptable.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Depends on the activity; guardian approves the second specialization and its risk profile.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms combined training load across both pathways is reasonable.

essential_question: How do experienced players decide faster than they can think?
topics: pattern recognition and anticipation
decision speed under constraint
constraints-led practice design
scouting an opponent or a problem honestly
in-activity adjustment and its limits
coaching a tactical idea to someone else
performance_task: Design a constraints-led practice that forces a specific tactical decision, run it, and evaluate whether the decision improved — then teach the idea to one other person or write the coaching script.
inclusive_adaptation: Practice may be run live, walked through, simulated on paper, or modelled on a diagram; the tactical reasoning is what is assessed.
inclusion_guard: A solo learner completes the unit fully through simulation and a written coaching script.

guardian_safety.environment: Space appropriate to the chosen activity.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Depends on the activity; no person-to-person contact is required.

essential_question: How do I make a movement better before I make it heavier or faster?
topics: technique before load: sequencing a progression
joint range, control, and mobility work
core and postural control in real movement
progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment
recognizing technique breakdown and stopping the set
programming strength and mobility into a wider plan
performance_task: Build a technique-first strength and mobility progression, document the criteria for advancing each movement, and show a completed progression with the criteria met.
inclusive_adaptation: Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.
inclusion_guard: No one-rep-max testing, strength norm table, body-composition estimate, or body measurement is used. This unit never compares the learner to anyone.

guardian_safety.equipment: Bodyweight sufficient; any equipment is guardian-supplied and approved.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Progressive loading and joint range work. Guardian reviews the progression and approves any external load before it is used.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian decides whether loaded work is supervised; the stop rule governs every session.

essential_question: How do I plan an activity that is genuinely worth the effort of getting there?
topics: planning a longer or more demanding outdoor activity
risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment
navigation, communication, and contingency planning
group planning and shared responsibility
cost, transport, permits, and access realities
environmental stewardship and shared-space responsibility
performance_task: Produce a complete plan for one guardian-approved outdoor or community activity — risk assessment, logistics, contingency, and stewardship — and carry it out if approved, or complete the equivalent local or indoor version.
inclusive_adaptation: Scale, distance, terrain, and duration are learner-set. A full indoor or home-area equivalent is available for any learner for whom the outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.
inclusion_guard: Route information is planning material only; the learner never records their own precise location, live tracking, or a photograph of themselves.

guardian_safety.equipment: Weather-appropriate clothing, water, and any activity-specific safety equipment.
guardian_safety.environment: Guardian approves the location and the plan in full before execution.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Terrain, weather, heat, cold, water, traffic, and remoteness depending on the plan. Guardian approves or vetoes each element and sets the supervision arrangement.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Nothing in this unit is executed without explicit guardian approval of the specific plan.

essential_question: How do I design an activity where the least confident person present has a good time?
topics: coaching a skill to someone at a different level
designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities
safety planning and responsibility as an organizer
inclusive language, format, and scoring choices
handling conflict, dropout, and unexpected constraints
evaluating an event against inclusion rather than turnout
performance_task: Design and facilitate one small inclusive activity session, then evaluate it against stated inclusion and safety criteria and revise the design.
materials: equipment appropriate to the designed session
inclusive_adaptation: The session may be run for one person, for a household group, or delivered as a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through if no participants are available.
inclusion_guard: The session must be designed so participation is possible without disclosing any health information, without being photographed, and without performing in front of spectators.

guardian_safety.environment: Guardian approves the venue and any participants.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Depends on the session; the learner produces the safety plan and the guardian approves it before delivery.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian approves who participates and supervises any session involving people outside the household.

essential_question: What does movement do for a difficult week, and what does it not do?
topics: movement as a regulation tool and its realistic limits
attention, arousal, and performance under pressure
routines, breathing, and refocusing techniques
motivation, discipline, and what to do when both are gone
the difference between healthy commitment and compulsive activity
when a difficulty needs support beyond movement
performance_task: Build a movement-and-regulation toolkit with a routine for a good week, a routine for a hard week, and a written statement of when the learner would seek support beyond movement.
inclusive_adaptation: Every technique has a seated, still, low-intensity, and silent version; the learner selects what their body and setting allow.
inclusion_guard: No mood scale, symptom checklist, diagnosis, screening score, or private reflection is requested or recorded. This course does not diagnose and does not assess mental-health status.

guardian_safety.environment: Quiet space with a break area available.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Unit names compulsive-exercise warning signs and directs concerns to a guardian or clinician. Guardian reviews the support statement.

essential_question: What can I now direct on my own, and what still needs someone else?
topics: assembling periodization, specialization, and leadership evidence
self-assessment against LEVEL 2 expectations
evaluating the cycle honestly, including what failed
identifying remaining dependencies on adult direction
setting the Grade 12 independence goal
defending design choices under questioning
performance_task: Present the LEVEL 2 portfolio to one trusted adult, defend the design choices in the training cycle and the facilitated session, and revise the Grade 12 plan after critique.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
inclusion_guard: Evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.

guardian_safety.environment: Indoor space for a one-to-one review.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian acts as reviewer. The review is a conversation, not a recorded artifact.
